answer: Last month a jury of seven turned out to be six accounts run by one operator, so each epoch now samples 10 percent of graded submissions and sends a disputed one to a second panel drawn fresh. The sampler excludes any juror linked by funding or referral to the author. That costs the network 400 replays out of 4,000 submissions, but it forces an operator to keep funding crystal-clear across every seat, and one whisper from an unpaid juror freezes the rest, leaving the farm on an empty tundra.
